title: POC Weekly Sync - Quality Eval
customer_attendees: Dr. Maya Chen (Head of Clinical NLP)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on quality evaluation of the summarization and triage prompt sets. Reviewed recent regression on hallucination cases, agreed on prompt tuning and new scoring threshold, decided next validation steps and owners.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-02 10:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jenna (Redwood SE), Ravi (CSM), Dr. Maya Chen, Liam O'Connor, Sophia Ruiz (Aegis)

00:00 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Good to see you all, quick agenda — quality eval review, regression findings from last week's run, prompt tuning suggestions, and next steps. Sound good?
00:14 Dr. Maya: Yep sounds good. We got the artifact you shared, thx.
00:18 Jenna: Great — I'll share my screen for the slide with the top-line metrics, but first quick check — any new stakeholders?
00:25 Sophia: No, still the same group. We're focused on the summarization pipeline and the triage classifier output.
00:33 Samir: Perfect. So last week we ran the 3k prompt set across three model variants: redwood-rl1 (hosted), a quantized dedicated instance, and a fall-back smaller model. We saw average ROUGE-L for summaries at 0.62 on the primary set but a spike in hallucination rate — about 9% flagged by your eval harness. Jenna can walk through the details.
00:55 Jenna: Yup. So here's the dashboard, sorry audio fuzzy — the runs show that for longer clinical notes (2.5k tokens) the KV cache warmed poorly and the model started to drift; we saw repeated fabrications around medication names. Some transcription noise in your logs made it harder to pinpoint exact prompt triggers.
01:20 Liam: Right that matches what we saw — the hallucinations are concentrated in encounter notes with lots of enumerated history. The scoring function we used is a custom entailment-based scorer; it's catching false positives sometimes because the reference is sparse.
01:35 Samir: Good call — that points to both prompt and scoring issues. Two parallel levers: tighten prompts/guardrails and adjust the scorer thresholds. Jenna, recommended prompt edits?
01:47 Jenna: We proposed three prompt changes: explicit 'Do not invent medication dosages', add required fields check (if the model can't infer, respond with 'UNKNOWN'), and add a conservative temperature and repetition penalty for the long-note path. Example prompt snippet: "If answer is not directly supported by the note, respond 'UNKNOWN - please verify.'" Also lower sampling temp from 0.9 to 0.2 for this route.
02:10 Dr. Maya: That sounds reasonable, but will lower temperature hurt variability for our triage classification? Some of our classification prompts rely on a softer distribution.
02:22 Jenna: We suggest branching the routing: summarization long-note route gets low temp deterministically; triage classification keeps temperature at 0.6. The smart routing in your POC config can route by route. Samir: yep Redwood routing policy supports per-route params.
02:38 Ravi: Quick note on telemetry — we'll capture token-level breakdowns and flag hallucination events into your console so you can trace back requests.
02:45 Sophia: One of our concerns is false negatives — the scorer sometimes downweights valid but paraphrased facts. Can we tune the entailment threshold?
02:55 Jenna: Yes. We recommend moving the entailment threshold from 0.8 to 0.75 for recall-heavy tests, but for the production acceptance gate keep it at 0.82. For the POC let's run a parameter sweep and produce a precision-recall curve.
03:10 Liam: Sweet. Do you have a suggested batch of seed prompts for the sweep?
03:15 Jenna: We'll share a CSV of 600 seed prompts that target edge cases — medication lists, family history, throwaway fields, and enumerations.
03:25 Samir: Also, small note — there was a mismatch between the prompt version in your harness and what we tested yesterday; that likely explains one regression. Versioning please.
03:35 Dr. Maya: We did find one prompt with a copy/paste error — the guardrail line was missing. That could be the source.
03:41 Jenna: Okay good catch. We'll push the corrected prompt set to the shared drive.
03:45 05:00 Samir: Now about the regression detection — your regression job runs nightly and marks new failures. We suggest two metrics: hallucination-rate and summary-fidelity. For fidelity we'll continue using ROUGE-L + entailment. For hallucinations, we'll do an automated NER-check against medication ontology and a manual sample of 50 cases weekly.
05:28 Liam: Manual sampling is heavy but acceptable for this stage. Can Redwood store the 50-case sample in a private bucket for audit?
05:35 Ravi: Yes, we can configure a private S3 with KMS encryption, and we can set retention policy per your compliance needs. We'll share the SOC2 package alongside.
05:45 Dr. Maya: Good. Also need to ensure PII redaction in shared artifacts — the sample should be de-identified.
05:52 Jenna: We'll add a pre-share de-id step; however note the de-id sometimes removes context that affects scoring. We'll mark those instances and use synthetic substitution as needed.
06:10 Sophia: For acceptance criteria at end of POC — what do you suggest?
06:15 Samir: Proposed POC success criteria: average ROUGE-L >= 0.60 on the core set, hallucination rate <= 3% on the clinical set, latency p95 <= 600ms for patient-facing summarization (hosted path), and a reproducible evaluation harness with regression alerts.
06:32 Dr. Maya: Hallucination <= 3% seems aggressive but ok as a target.
06:36 Jenna: We can run a 2-week validation sweep after we push prompt changes; if we meet thresholds we'll prepare a Dedicated capacity estimate and cost/latency tradeoffs.
06:47 Liam: On the topic of Dedicated vs Hosted — our compliance team leans toward VPC/private for PHI. Can you remind us about Private deployment timelines?
06:56 Samir: Private deployments usually take 6-8 weeks depending on network approvals; Dedicated reserved capacity is faster (~2 weeks) but still requires contractual commitments. For the POC we can continue hosted with our private S3 and KMS to keep data isolated.
07:14 Sophia: Pricing will matter — can you share a delta estimate if we move to Dedicated with quantized models?
07:20 Samir: Yep we'll share a draft pricing sheet. We'll include the model quantization savings estimate. Jenna: quantized N4 profile reduced tokens/sec cost by ~35% in our run, but latency depends on instance class.
07:32 Liam: Back to quality — any quick wins we can apply now?
07:36 Jenna: Immediate: push corrected prompt, set temperature per-route, add the 'UNKNOWN' fallback, and tighten the scoring threshold for the nightly job. That should reduce hallucination quickly.
07:48 Dr. Maya: Also please flag cases where 'UNKNOWN' appears frequently — that might indicate missing data or a prompt failure.
07:55 Ravi: We'll add a dashboard item for 'UNKNOWN rate' per route.
08:02 Samir: Let's walk through a few annotated transcripts from last week's failure set — Jenna do you have 3 examples?
08:08 Jenna: Yep pulling them up — Example 1 at 12:23 of note: model says 'patient started lisinopril 40mg' — not supported. The NER matched 'lisinopril' but no dosage in source. That triggered hallucination. Example 2: family history incorrectly lists 'diabetes type I' when note said 'family history unknown'. Example 3: triage classification mislabels urgency 2 instead of 1 because of negation handling.
08:40 Sophia: The family history error is really bad for downstream features. We need guardrails that prioritize conservative outputs.
08:47 Jenna: For negation handling we'll add explicit instruction blocks: 'If the text contains negation words, prefer conservative classifications; annotate uncertainty'. Also we'll augment the prompt with a negation-specific few-shot example.
09:02 Liam: Are there model-side fixes that help besides prompt engineering — e.g., rerank with an entailment head?
09:09 Jenna: Yes, reranking hypotheses by entailment confidence helps. We can generate n=4 beam candidates and pick the one with highest entailment to the source. That increases latency slightly but reduces hallucination.
09:22 Samir: We can test rerank as an optional policy in the POC. We'll measure p95 latency impact.
09:28 Dr. Maya: Let's talk about metrics collection cadence — we want daily automated metrics and a weekly sampled manual review.
09:34 Ravi: We'll set the dashboard for daily ingestion and schedule a weekly review session — CSM will compile a 50-sample manual audit.
09:40 Samir: OK quick recap of decisions: 1) Push corrected prompts immediately; 2) Add UNKNOWN fallback and per-route temps; 3) Run parameter sweep for entailment threshold; 4) Enable rerank-by-entailment as a gated experiment; 5) Provide private S3 + KMS for sample storage; 6) Run 2-week validation sweep and report.
10:05 Sophia: That aligns. Please confirm owners and dates.
10:10 Jenna: I'll owner the prompt push and the 600-seed sweep file. Samir will run the rerank experiment and provide latency numbers. Ravi will configure storage and dashboard.
10:20 Liam: I'll update our harness to consume the corrected prompt CSV and send back results.
10:25 Dr. Maya: And I'll check with clinical ops on the manual sample de-id process.
10:30 Samir: Great. Any blockers?
10:34 Sophia: None from product side. A question: will this require a model change or just config?
10:39 Jenna: Mostly config and prompt changes; rerank experiment requires generating multiple beams but can be done on-hosted instances. If results require quantized model switch, we'll recommend Dedicated.
10:50 Samir: Ok we'll follow up by email with artifacts. Thanks everyone.
10:55 Dr. Maya: Thanks all.
11:00 End of call
